criteria.justification: The response immediately commits to “roll back (disable/feature-flag off) the new integration launch right now” and reinforces this with a concrete first action to direct engineering to disable or revert it.

It explicitly identifies rollback as reversible because the integration can be relaunched after a proper fix, while contrasting that with customer trust damage and support load from leaving the issue live, which are “not obviously reversible.”

The response directly weighs compounding incorrect signals, support burden, and trust erosion against the reputational and scheduling cost of pausing a publicly announced feature, concluding that the latter is temporary and recoverable.
It does not propose rushing a speculative fix; instead, it characterizes rollback as a “known, bounded action” and reserves the several-day, well-tested fix for a follow-up relaunch.
Beyond rollback, it specifies verifying recovery, notifying affected and integration customers, asynchronously escalating to the manager, and opening a proper-fix, relaunch, and retrospective track.
